findings.title: Public findMany() method removed without updating/checking callers
findings.body: The `findMany(findManyArgs)` method that previously returned fully-typed Prisma results has been removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. This PR only touches `insightsBooking.ts` and its test file, but `InsightsBookingService.findMany` is a public API that is very likely consumed elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. insights trpc routers/handlers). Removing this method without updating or even searching for its call sites will break compilation or runtime behavior for any consumer still calling `.findMany(...)`. The PR should either keep a `findMany`-equivalent wrapper around the new raw-SQL conditions, or update all call sites in the same change.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests removed with no replacement
findings.body: The previous `describe("Caching", ...)` block, which verified that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return cached (identical) results on repeated calls, was deleted entirely in this PR. The service still implements `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` caching logic (lines 49-50, 84-95 of insightsBooking.ts), but after this change there is no test coverage verifying that caching still works correctly with the new `Prisma.sql` return type, leaving a regression risk undetected if caching logic breaks (e.g., due to object identity issues with `Prisma.Sql` instances).

findings.title: PR description misrepresents scope of change
findings.body: The PR description states the production code conversion to `Prisma.sql` was "previously converted in the service implementation" and that this PR "updates ... tests to work with the new Prisma.sql format", implying `insightsBooking.ts` is unchanged context. However, the diff shows substantial production logic changes in `insightsBooking.ts` itself (converting Prisma object-filter WHERE clauses to raw SQL, removing `findMany`, renaming types, changing return types of `buildAuthorizationConditions`/`buildFilterConditions`/`getBaseConditions`). Mischaracterizing this as a test-only fix could cause reviewers to under-scrutinize an actually risky production change to authorization-critical SQL generation.
